doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Jukkis Uotila's Introspection and Don Thompson's date
summary: They recall a Finnish record date with Frisell, Formanek and Samuels, and Don Thompson's Canadian date with Claude Ranger.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Here’s the first of a couple dates you did over the years with our friend Jukkis Uotila.
Yes. This is – he called me.
European thing, called me, “I’m Jukkis. I’m from Finland.” Dave Samuels? Dave Friedman? Something like that?
Yeah. Dave Samuels, Formanek, Frisell – a very young Bill Frisell, probably.
Yes, yes. I forgot that Bill was on that. Jukkis – I didn’t know Jukkis. What’s that? Hell of a musician here. What the heck is this about? I had no idea what Finland was.
One of my – a great European drummer.
Yeah, he’s great, killer, a great musician.
Here’s one with a Canadian band, with Don Thompson and Claude Ranger, plus Steve LaSpina on bass.

The legendary Claude Ranger, who’s disappeared. This is Don Thompson recording and playing at the same time. Hitting the microphone and coming into the studio. It is his label called From Bebop to Now.
I used him. He played vibes, bass, and piano. That’s a musician of musicians. It’s up there.
Yeah. A world class piano player and bass player and vibes player.
